pitfalls:
Coordinate-normalization pitfalls to watch (the MiniMax-M3 problem is one symptom of several):

1. Normalized vs pixel space differs by API and is the #1 source of drift. Always multiply or divide by the model's exact denominator before applying:
   - AWS Textract BoundingBox (Left/Top/Width/Height): floats in [0,1] of page W/H. Polygon Points: same scale. Multiply by image W,H. [docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/text-location.html]
   - Google Document AI: BoundingPoly exposes BOTH vertices[] (pixel ints) AND normalizedVertices[] (floats in [0,1]). Each tool surfaces only one — pick explicitly. [cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta3/Document]
   - Google Cloud Vision (legacy OCR): normalizedVertices only [0,1]. [docs.cloud.google.cn/.../ocr/rpc/google.cloud.vision.v1]
   - Mistral OCR 4/4.1 blocks[].top_left_x, top_left_y, bottom_right_x, bottom_right_y: PIXEL coordinates (no scaling). Page dimensions returned separately in page.dimensions. [docs.mistral.ai/studio/document-processing/basic_ocr]
   - Gemini bounding-box detection: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] ints NORMALIZED to a fixed 0..1000 grid regardless of aspect ratio. [cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/bounding-box-detection]
   - GPT-5.x vision: no native bbox; user must define [x_min,y_min,x_max,y_max] in a fixed 0..999 grid via prompt + json_schema. OpenAI cookbook warns to use Code Interpreter for reliability because a single-pass call drifts. [developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/multimodal/document_and_multimodal_understanding_tips]
   - Qwen-VL-OCR advanced_recognition (qwen-vl-ocr-2025-08-28+): PIXEL coordinates in two formats: 4-vertex polygon [x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3,x4,y4] OR rotated rect [cx,cy,w,h,angle]. Top-left origin. [alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-vl-ocr]
   - Qwen2.5/3-VL raw (non-OCR endpoint): [x1,y1,x2,y2] in 0..999 normalized grid. [deepwiki.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/5.1-ocr-and-document-processing]
   - dots.ocr (rednote-hilab/dots.ocr 1.7B; dots.mocr 3B): bbox format [x1,y1,x2,y2] but in the Qwen2VLImageProcessor-RESIZED coordinate space (width*height <= 11,289,600 px, multiples of 28). Must apply the smart_resize inverse mapping back to original pixel coords — naive copying gives ±10% drift identical in shape to MiniMax-M3's failure. [huggingface.co/davanstrien/dots.ocr-1.5]
   - PaddleOCR-VL: returns detection boxes in pixel coords via PP-DocLayoutV3 (axis-aligned) or multi-point polygons in PP-DocLayoutV3 / RT-DocLayout (PaddleOCR-VL-1.5). [arxiv.org/html/2510.14528v4; arxiv.org/pdf/2606.23344v1]
   - Granite-Docling-258M: emits DocTags with <loc_*> normalized tokens (0..999 grid like Qwen), must be un-normalized to pixel. [huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-docling-258M]
   - Surya OCR 2: per-block JSON, normalized pixel coords; same handling. [github.com/datalab-to/surya]
   - GLM-OCR: layout in PP-DocLayoutV3 coords (pixel, polygon-capable in v3); text bbox in pixel space. [arxiv.org/html/2603.10910]

2. The Mistral OCR 4.1 story is a textbook example of the failure mode MiniMax-M3 has: on dense, marked-up Russian documents (stamps, hand-filled form fields, highlighted clauses), earlier OCR/VLM blocks can drift several pixels, swallow two adjacent paragraphs into one box, or nest one figure inside another. Mistral explicitly engineered OCR 4.1 (Aug 13 2026) to fix 'no more box drift' and 'no more nested images' on exactly that workload. Any tool chosen for Russian bureaucratic documents with stamps/highlights/handwriting should be one that has been audited for this — Mistral OCR 4.1 is the only one with a public release-note fix. [pasqualepillitteri.it/.../mistral-ocr-4-1-bounding-boxes-marked-up-pages]

3. Language coverage — Cyrillic is not universal:
   - AWS Textract explicitly does NOT support Cyrillic. Supported OCR languages are English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese. Forms/tables/queries English-only. Russian docs will silently degrade to garbage or empty. [aws.amazon.com/textract/faqs]
   - Azure Document Intelligence Read supports Cyrillic; Layout model supports 309+ languages including Cyrillic. (Confirm region availability before deployment.)
   - Google Document AI Form Parser / OCR supports Cyrillic. [Google docs]
   - Hosted VLMs (Gemini, GPT-5.x, Qwen3-VL, GLM-OCR, Mistral OCR 4) all support Russian; quality varies (Gemini 2.5/3 Pro strongest on Slavic historical text per the arxiv.org/abs/2510.06743 historical-DH benchmark; Qwen3-VL best among open weights).
   - PaddleOCR-VL: Cyrillic edit-distance 0.109 on its multilingual benchmark (lowest among major models). [arxiv.org/html/2510.14528v4]
   - dots.ocr / dots.mocr: explicitly multilingual, top SOTA on XDocParse (126 languages incl. Russian). [arxiv.org/html/2512.02498v4]
   - Surya OCR 2: internal Russian benchmark score 88.8% (top-3 widely-spoken language). [github.com/datalab-to/surya]
   - olmOCR 2: olmOCR-Bench is English-only; do not deploy on Russian without testing.

4. Quantization pitfalls on the 6GB Turing GPU:
   - dots.ocr (1.7B / 3B): needs 7GB FP16. On 6GB must run Q4 (~2GB) or use am009's Docker fork (float32 Turing support, tested on 2080Ti 22GB). [github.com/am009/dots.ocr]
   - PaddleOCR-VL (0.9B): officially minimum 12GB (RTX 3060). On 6GB you need to either drop the PP-DocLayoutV3 stage and run PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B recognition-only (set use_layout_detection=False), or quantize. vLLM raw FP16 single request is ~3.6 s/page on 8GB; batch-1 should fit 6GB at gpu_memory_utilization≈0.85 with enforce_eager=True. [adityamangal98.medium.com/paddleocr-vl-with-vllm-a-complete-performance-benchmark-76-faster-2d1ddad90365]
   - Surya OCR 2 (0.65B): GGUF build runs via llama.cpp on consumer GPUs incl. 6GB. Easiest local pick. [huggingface.co/datalab-to/surya-ocr-2-gguf]
   - GLM-OCR (0.9B): with PP-DocLayoutV3 on CPU and GLM-OCR 0.9B on GPU 6GB is the documented layout-on-CPU mode; fits. [github.com/zai-org/GLM-OCR]
   - Mistral OCR 4 / 4.1: API only, or self-hosted in a container (≥24GB VRAM recommended for throughput; small batch possible at 16GB).
   - olmOCR 2: 7B FP8 model. 8GB FP8 minimum; 6GB risky. [huggingface.co/allenai/olmOCR-2-7B-1025]
   - GPT-5.x / Gemini / Qwen-VL-OCR (hosted): no GPU constraint.

5. Coordinate-system rotatability: dense-table bboxes that aren't rotated rectangles lose fidelity on rotated scans. PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 (PP-DocLayoutV3 multi-point), Qwen-VL-OCR (rotate_rect), and Mistral OCR 4.1 all expose rotated/polygon boxes; AWS Textract/Google Document AI expose a polygon[]; everything else is axis-aligned only.

6. VLM bbox drift: Gemini and GPT-5 with a one-shot prompt for full-document layout will silently drop fine-grained bboxes or hallucinate them. Cookbook-recommended fix is two-pass: (a) detect text regions, (b) crop + OCR each region for stable geometry.
recommendations:
Top-3 recommendation, ranked for Russian bureaucratic docs (stamps, dense forms, ЕГРН-style tables, rotated scans, handwriting, stylized fonts) on a 6GB GPU with budget for tokens but not for a second GPU:

1) Mistral OCR 4.1 (hosted API; self-hosted container if data-sovereignty required)
   - Why: it is the ONLY release as of Q3 2026 with an explicit, public, post-hoc engineering fix for exactly the bbox-drift problem the user describes ('bbox coordinates drift ±10% from actual image — geometry unreliable'). 170 languages including Russian and East-European Cyrillic. Pixel-coordinate boxes (top_left_x/y, bottom_right_x/y) in page.dimensions — no normalization ambiguity. Block-level + word-level confidence scores let you gate low-confidence geometry. Tables as HTML. Reads PDF/DOCX/PPTX/OpenDocument natively. $4/1k pages standard, $2/1k pages Batch (halves cost for offline batches), $5/1k pages with Document AI annotations. [docs.mistral.ai/studio/document-processing/basic_ocr; mistral.ai/news/ocr-4/]
   - Pitfalls to watch: occasional hallucinated sentences mid-document on adversarial pages; catch via the new confidence_scores_granularity='block' filter and route low-confidence blocks to Tesseract + Surya fallback. Russian-language quality is strong in v4 (omnilingual benchmark internal Crawl Multilingual .98 leader), but for Slavic historical/handwriting edge cases (см. arxiv.org/abs/2510.06743), supplement with a handwriting specialist on the failing subset.

2) PaddleOCR-VL / PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 (self-hosted on GTX 1660 6GB with caveats)
   - Why: best multilingual SOTA in its weight class (0.9B params). Cyrillic edit-distance 0.109 on the in-house multilingual benchmark (lowest among the major open models). PP-DocLayoutV3 produces multi-point polygons and pixel-coord boxes that survive skew/warp (14.11 pp improvement on the Skew subset of Real5-OmniDocBench) — important for rotated Russian scans. 109 languages including Russian. OmniDocBench v1.5 composite 94.50 (PaddleOCR-VL-1.5). Apache-2.0. [arxiv.org/html/2510.14528v4; arxiv.org/html/2601.21957]
   - GPU reality: official minimum is 12GB (RTX 3060). On 6GB Turing you must (a) run PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B only with use_layout_detection=False and accept ~273 s/page in raw transformers mode, OR (b) use vLLM with gpu_memory_utilization≈0.85 + enforce_eager=True to get ~3.6 s/page single / 0.23 s/page at batch-16 on 8GB — the official Paddle docs warn CC 7.0 (Turing) is 'prone to timeouts or OOM' so expect tuning pain, OR (c) use the layout stage on CPU (RT-DocLayout/PP-DocLayoutV3 is small enough at 33M params to run on CPU at 13 ms/page) and the VLM stage on 6GB GPU. The third option is the realistic path. [github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR/issues/16823; arxiv.org/pdf/2606.23344v1; adityamangal98.medium.com/paddleocr-vl-with-vllm-a-complete-performance-benchmark-76-faster-2d1ddad90365]
   - Pair with PaddleOCR's PP-DocLayoutV3 detection + RT-DocLayout reading-order if you want robust scan geometry independent of the VLM stage.

3) dots.ocr (1.7B) / dots.mocr (3B) (self-hosted; HF + vLLM)
   - Why: 1.7B multilingual document parser with explicit [x1,y1,x2,y2] layout bboxes per element. Strongest open-weight performer on the 126-language XDocParse benchmark (+7.4 over Gemini-2.5-Pro on Overall Edit distance, –54% Text Edit distance). dots.mocr 3B improves further (OmniDocBench v1.5 Text-Edit 0.031, Reading-Order 0.029; olmOCR-Bench 83.9). Single VLM does layout+content, no error propagation between pipeline stages. [arxiv.org/html/2512.02498v4; github.com/rednote-hilab/dots.ocr; codesota.com/ocr/dots-ocr]
   - Critical pitfall: returned bbox is in the Qwen2VLImageProcessor-RESIZED coordinate space (max 11,289,600 px, multiples of 28). MUST apply the smart_resize inverse scale to recover original-image coords — skipping this step gives the same ±10% drift MiniMax-M3 exhibits. Use huggingface.co/davanstrien/dots.ocr-1.5 reference smart_resize() function. [huggingface.co/davanstrien/dots.ocr-1.5]
   - GPU reality: FP16 needs 7GB. On 6GB use the Q4_K_M GGUF (2GB) via llama.cpp, OR use the am009/dots.ocr Docker fork (explicit Turing/20-series fp32 support, tested on 2080Ti 22GB; on 6GB run at fp32 with reduced image size). vLLM has official dots.ocr integration since v0.11.0. [github.com/am009/dots.ocr; github.com/rednote-hilab/dots.ocr]

Honourable mentions (use as supplementary engines, not primary):
- Google Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite ($0.33/1k pages) or 2.5 Flash ($1.95/1k pages): cheapest hosted path, normalized 0..1000 grid via responseSchema, excellent Russian; loses to Mistral on dense-table bbox fidelity because it has no audited 'box-drift fix'. Good for high-volume clean-text-only extraction where bbox tolerance is loose. [docuocr.com/gemini-ocr-pricing; cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/bounding-box-detection]
- Azure Document Intelligence Layout (~$10/1k pages): 309+ languages incl. Cyrillic, polygon bboxes in normalizedVertices, enterprise-grade SLAs. Slower than Mistral/VLM on novel layouts. [docuocr.com/azure-document-intelligence-pricing]
- Qwen-VL-OCR via Alibaba DashScope (qwen-vl-ocr-2025-08-28+): native pixel-coord polygons, rotated rectangles, multilingual incl. Russian. Good Russian text accuracy. API only. [alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-vl-ocr]
- Surya OCR 2 (0.65B) + TrOCR cyrillic-trocr/trocr-base-handwritten-ru: the right lightweight combo for handwritten Cyrillic sub-pass on the 6GB GPU; use the GGUF build. [github.com/datalab-to/surya; huggingface.co/cyrillic-trocr]

Explicit disqualifications for this task:
- AWS Textract: no Cyrillic support, Russian docs will return wrong/empty text. Hard NO.
- olmOCR 2: English-only training/benchmark; will degrade on Russian. olmOCR-Bench pass rate 82.4 but with no Cyrillic.
- Granite-Docling-258M: 'optimized for Latin-script documents', Cyrillic only experimental — explicitly limited.
- Nougat: math/paper model; Russian text quality is low; slow.
- GPT-5 vision for layout: needs Code-Interpreter pass for stable geometry and balloons cost; Mistral/GLM-OCR offer better geometric guarantees per ruble.
- Mistral OCR 2 (mistral-ocr-2505): superseded by OCR 3 → OCR 4 → OCR 4.1; the OCR-2 era was when geometry drift was worst. Move off it.

Suggested production stack for the user's scenario (RU docs + 6GB GPU + budget for tokens + need accurate bbox):
- Primary (text quality + bbox): Mistral OCR 4.1 API ($4/1k pages, $2 batch) for any document needing citable geometry; route low-confidence blocks via confidence_scores_granularity='block' to a local fallback.
- Local fallback on GTX 1660 (privacy / cost-savings): PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 with PP-DocLayoutV3 on CPU + PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B on GPU; or dots.ocr-1.7B at Q4_K_M via llama.cpp. Smart_resize the bbox output before merging into the PDF text layer.
- Handwritten Cyrillic sub-pass: Surya OCR 2 (0.65B GGUF) for layout+text + TrOCR cyrillic-trocr for line-level confirmation. No bbox-level guarantee for TrOCR — keep it as verification, not geometry source.
- Old-style/budget fallback: keep tesseract rus as third-tier safety net (already in stack, fast+free+mid quality); chain after Mistral/Paddle reject low-confidence pages.
